summary: Describes how to tunnel Frame Relay over L2TPv3, covering frame encapsulation, virtual-circuit creation and deletion, and status change notification. L2TPv3 tunnels data link protocols over IP networks. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Frame Relay was an older kind of data line. This shows how to carry its traffic inside ordinary IP packets, like sending a small box inside a larger one.

questions: what is frame relay over l2tpv3
what is a frame relay pseudowire
how does l2tpv3 report frame relay pvc status
what is the circuit status avp
subtitle: How to carry Frame Relay virtual circuits across an IP network using L2TPv3 pseudowires.

tldr.problem: Service providers wanted to offer Frame Relay PVC service across an IP packet network, and the L2TPv3 base protocol does not say how to carry Frame Relay specifically.
tldr.mechanism: Each Frame Relay PVC maps to one L2TPv3 session. The frame is sent whole, minus the HDLC flags and FCS, while a Circuit Status AVP and the SLI message report whether the PVC is ACTIVE or INACTIVE.
tldr.outcome: The document defines the Frame Relay pseudowire type, three result codes and one new AVP. It was later updated by RFC 5641.

today: RFC 4591 is a Proposed Standard and has been updated by RFC 5641. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
RFC 3931 defines the base L2TPv3 protocol for tunneling Layer 2 traffic over IP. RFC 4591 adds what is needed to tunnel Frame Relay that way. The emulated circuits are called Frame Relay Pseudowires (FRPWs).

This RFC works in a virtual-circuit to virtual-circuit mode. It covers frame encapsulation, creating and deleting PVCs, and telling the peer when a PVC changes state. Carrying a whole port instead is done with HDLC pseudowires from RFC 4349. Switched Virtual Circuits (SVCs) and Switched/Soft Permanent Virtual Circuits (SPVCs) are out of scope.
sections.eli5: Some old phone-company style data lines used Frame Relay. This paper says how to send each of those lines' traffic through the Internet inside special packets.

sections.title: Control Connection and Session Setup
sections.content:
First an L2TPv3 control connection MUST be set up. The SCCRQ and SCCRP messages MUST list the Frame Relay DLCI pseudowire type, 0x0001, in the Pseudowire Capabilities List. Each endpoint (an LCCE) must identify itself with a globally unique value, by default the Router ID AVP; the Hostname AVP MAY be used instead.

Creating a PVC leads to an L2TP session through the standard three-way handshake. An LCCE MAY start it as soon as the PVC is created, or wait until the PVC is ACTIVE, which delays using L2TP resources until needed. The ICRQ MUST carry the Pseudowire Type AVP (attribute type 68) with the Frame Relay type and the Circuit Status AVP, and MUST carry the Remote End ID AVP to say which PVC is meant. At minimum an endpoint must support an unstructured four-octet value there.

If the far end has not provisioned the PVC, it answers with a CDN, and the initiator SHOULD retry periodically, with a configurable period and maximum number of retries. An ICRQ or ICRP MAY be sent while the PVC is INACTIVE, provided the Circuit Status AVP says so and an SLI follows when it becomes ACTIVE.
sections.eli5: Before two routers can share a line, they say hello, agree they both do Frame Relay, and name the line they mean. If one of them has never heard of that line, it says no and the other can try again later.

sections.title: PVC Status, Teardown and Header Length
sections.content:
If a PVC is deleted, the session MUST be torn down with a CDN. This RFC adds three result codes: 17 (PVC deleted permanently), 18 (PVC INACTIVE for an extended period) and 19 (mismatched Frame Relay header length).

Status changes travel in the SLI message, which is sent reliably over the control channel. It MUST be sent whenever the circuit status changes, apart from the initial ICRQ, ICRP and CDN. An LCCE that takes part in the Q.933 Annex A status procedures with its attached system MUST send an SLI when it sees a local status change, and an LCCE receiving one SHOULD pass the update on towards its own Frame Relay side. The L2TP Hello facility gives every session basic dead peer detection.

The Circuit Status AVP (attribute type 71) is a 16-bit mask where only the two lowest bits are defined: N (New, 1 for a new PVC) and A (Active, 1 for ACTIVE). Reserved bits MUST be 0 when sent and are ignored on receipt.

The Frame Relay Header Length AVP (attribute type 85) tells the peer how long the Frame Relay header is: 2 or 4 octets. Both ends MUST agree. A mismatch means the session is torn down with result code 19. If the AVP is absent, a 2-byte header is assumed.
sections.eli5: The two routers keep telling each other whether the line is working or broken, using a little note with two yes-or-no boxes. They also have to agree on how big the address label on each frame is, or they hang up.

sections.title: Data Packet Encapsulation
sections.content:
The Frame Relay frame is carried in its entirety, but without the opening and closing HDLC flags and the frame check sequence (FCS). Bit stuffing is undone. The L2TPv3 session header is as in RFC 3931, and if sequencing or other features need an L2-Specific Sublayer, the Default format MUST be used.

The Frame Relay header holds the DLCI plus four flag bits. C/R is passed on unchanged and MUST NOT be changed by the LCCE. FECN and BECN (forward and backward congestion notification) MAY be set by the LCCE to warn end users of congestion and must never be cleared. DE (discard eligible) MAY be set by a policing function and also must never be cleared. An LCCE that does not support FECN, BECN or DE passes the bit unchanged.

The two-octet header is REQUIRED. The four-octet header is OPTIONAL. A three-octet header is out of scope. The egress LCCE rewrites the DLCI and regenerates the FCS.
sections.eli5: The router takes the Frame Relay message, peels off the outer wrapping, and puts what is left into an IP packet. Little flag bits on the message say "traffic jam ahead" or "throw me away first if you must", and the router must never erase those warnings.

sections.title: Sequencing and MTU
sections.content:
Sequencing MAY be enabled for FRPWs, using the mechanisms of RFC 3931. When it is enabled, the pseudowire MUST request the Default L2-Specific Sublayer. If the data does not need strict ordering, such as IP, sequencing SHOULD NOT be enabled.

Encapsulation makes each packet N bytes longer than the Frame Relay frame without flags and FCS. N is built from the session header (a 4-octet Flags/Ver/Res field for UDP only, a 4-octet Session ID), a cookie of 0, 4 or 8 octets, and a 0 or 4 octet L2-Specific Sublayer. That gives N = 4 to 16 over IP and N = 16 to 28 over UDP, not counting the IP header. The maximum frame size is limited by the network MTU unless fragmentation and reassembly are used.
sections.eli5: Wrapping a message in an extra envelope makes it a bit bigger, so the packet must still fit through the pipe. If order matters, you number the packets so they can be put back in line.

sections.title: Applicability, Security and IANA
sections.content:
The applicability statement says an FRPW allows a provider to offer a PVC-based Frame Relay service across an IP packet-switched network. Mapping is one-to-one between a PVC and an FRPW. Quality of service such as throughput (CIR), committed burst size (bc), excess burst size (be) and priority can be provided by using the QoS features of the LCCEs and the underlying network.

On security, the RFC says Frame Relay over L2TPv3 is subject to the considerations in RFC 3931, and that carrying Frame Relay adds none beyond those for other data link types.

IANA allocated pseudowire type 0x0001 (Frame Relay DLCI), Result Code AVP values 17, 18 and 19, and AVP attribute 85 (Frame Relay Header Length).
sections.eli5: The rules about who may trust whom are the same as for other kinds of lines carried this way. The paper also asks the Internet's number keeper to reserve a few numbers for this job.

fields.desc: Set to 0 by the sender, ignored by the receiver.
